recipes.name: Chocolate Banana Cream Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (9 inch) deep dish pie crust, baked and cooled
1 (3.5 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Combine chocolate, 1 tablespoon milk, and butter or margarine in a medium, microwave safe bowl. Microwave on high for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds. Stir until chocolate is completely melted. Spread evenly in pie crust.
Pour 1 1/2 cups milk into a large bowl. Add pudding mix, and beat with wire whisk for 2 minutes. Stir in 1 1/2 cups coconut. Spoon over banana slices in crust.
Spread whipped topping over pie. Sprinkle with toasted coconut. Refrigerate 4 hours, or until set. Store in refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Banana Cream Pie
raw_recipe.description: A creamy layered pie; the layers include chocolate, bananas, and vanilla pudding with coconut. Easy, and very yummy.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious! I went along with a lot of the modifications; I went with the graham cracker crust instead of the regular pie crust, I used banana pudding instead of vanilla, and I added an extra ounce of chocolate. I also used semisweet chocolate chips instead of squares. It ended up being perfect. I didn't feel like turning on the oven just to toast the coconut, so I used 1/2 tsp of butter and toasted the coconut in a pan.

Loved by all. I made several modifications to fit our family's needs. First, I reduced the amount of shredded coconut to 1 cup. I also used a large package of vanilla instant pudding (5 ounces) and used 2 cups of milk to be in proportion with the pudding. For the chocolate, I found that we had no squares, so I used semisweet chocolate chips (1/2 cup). Finally, instead of putting the whipped cream on before refrigerating, I put on a dollop as I served each piece. However, I don't think that the whipped cream (or Cool Whip) is absolutely necessary if you are looking to cut a few calories. This is a great recipe and by far the best banana cream pie recipe I have ever had. The chocolate layer adds a lot.

I cant imagine why anyone wouldnt love this. I used a Marie Calander frozen pie crust -excellent. Added a little extra chocolate and a touch of dark rum; maybe a 1/2 tsp....It really added nice flavor. Extra Bananas. White chocolate pudding, because thats all I had on hand, and toasted the coconut. On a side note; I refrigerated pudding so it would thicken up and then added coconut in with a wire wisk. I used only 1c of coconut in the pie and topped it off with remaining...Amazing!

I've made this pie a few times before and made the suggested edits that other reviewers have made (graham cracker crust, more chocolate, but I added more coconut b/c I love coconut). It turns out so well my fiance asks for it every birthday. But this year, I was so busy I didn't have a chance to buy coconut so I just winged my own edits. In addition to 3 oz of chocolate, I added 5 tablespoons of peanut butter and a splash of soy milk and melted it in the microwave. Then I spread it on the bottom of the pie crust and crumbled about 10 peanut butter-filled pretzels over it before the banana slices went in. It was awesome!!!

This is my boyfriends favorite pie, and sometimes I must make two just to get a piece for myself! Everyone who has ever tried it raves and raves about how fantastic it is! I sometimes use a little less coconut, and often make my own crust with the french pastry crust recipe from this site, with a little cinnamon (1 tsp) added to the crust. I used hershey dark chocolate baking squares for the chocolate in this recipe and always make my own whipped cream with sugar, vanilla, and stabilizer. Always turns out perfect!! A must make pie for any occassion! You can dress it up nicely by piping the cream on top or making chocolate shavings to place around the edges.

made this last night after reading the suggestions, i used a graham wafer crust, omitted the coconut, used banana pudding instead of vanilla and doubled the chocolate... I waited to add the cool whip until the pie had cooled... i put it in the fridge to harden then added the cool whip some cocoa powder and topped it off with chocolate chips for the garnish!! Absolutely delicious!!!! Everyone loves it!!

Very good, I made a few changes. I used an extra servings size graham cracker crust, 3 bananas, banana pudding, 2 tbsp milk, 1 tbsp butter and 1/2 cup chocolate chips. Also I decreased the coconut to 1/2 cup. I made double layers as in lasagna. Turned out great

Oh my! This was fantastic...I used dark chocolate and a premade grahm cracker crust. I had some strawberries so I added a layer of those. I skipped the Coconut as I'm not a big fan. For extra decadence I melted some dark chocolage and drizzled generously over the top of each piece right before serving. The contrast between bitter and sweet was wonderful!

Delicious, quick, and easy!
I like using an Oreo Crust and doubling the chocolate.
Also, Banana Cream Pie Pudding mix makes this extra yummy!
I'm not a super fan of coconut, so I usually just leave it out. 
I made this for a yummy summer treat at the lake and my aunt couldn't stop helping herself to this scrumptious pie.
doubled the chocolate layer as it barely covered the bottom of the pie. It was delicious. I will share this receipe with my friends

Loved the combination of flavors in this recipe. I doubled the banana and the chocolate (semi-sweet chips). I don't think I would use cool whip again, though. It oozed off of the pie and made a mess. Next time, I will refrigerate the pie first and then add fresh whipped cream at the last minute.
Came out so good! I've made this several times since! Easy & perfect every time.

I followed the recipe exactly except for the coconut which I completely omitted because I read that many other reviewers did the same and it turned out great for them. For me, it turned out like soup:( The only thing I'm thinking is I used oat milk, is that what could have caused the issue? Otherwise, maybe I didn't beat the pudding mixture hard enough? How firm is the pudding mixture supposed to be before putting it into the pie crust? I gave it two stars bc the chocolate mix and the pudding mix both tasted delicious at least.

This pie was a great success! I followed the recipe, but did add chocolate shards to the top and sprinkled toasted coconut around the edges of the crust. I brought it to a small get together and there was only one small slice left. Everyone including myself thought it was delicious.
Delicious! Next time I would use less coconut.
This has turned into a holiday staple in my house. I have been making it for 6 years. Every time i make it for a holiday party, work gathering or BBQ it's always a hit.
The kids didn't care for it (why is there crunchy stuff in here!), but I thought it was good for what it is...Quick banana pie that's not from scratch, but it gets the job done.
A delihtful change from regular banana.
I made it just like the recipe and it was delicious, thank you for sharing it!
Came out soupy for the 1st take. Second take- I added more bananas and tried to make the vanilla pudding a little thicker. Looks good!
